source.stem: Decide whether the following statements are correct. Mark “√” for correct answers and “×” for wrong answers. (1) Objects that can move must be living things.

hinge.title: Decide whether Earth's ability to support life comes from one feature or from linked life-supporting conditions.

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: Earth is the same as its neighbouring term in this chapter, so the decision does not change.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: The decision still holds even if we ignore this condition: This claim is about life as we know it on Earth.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: places and requirements for living beings -> life can grow and survive happens first, and that produces linked surface conditions and resources.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: This rule applies even when This claim is about life as we know it on Earth is not true.

intelligence.enrichment: Earth supports life because a thin surface layer contains living things and Earth provides air, water, soil, shelter, food, and other connected living and non-living conditions. linked surface conditions and resources -> places and requirements for living beings -> life can grow and survive The learner correctly uses the chapter relationship: Earth supports life because a thin surface layer contains living things and Earth provides air, water, soil, shelter, food, and other connected living and non-living conditions. Earth supports life simply because it has water, so other surface conditions do not matter.
